units: Studies how a self-modifying system can continue to be corrected by reality after gaining ability to modify itself.
GRA is explicitly not a general theory of intelligence, goals, or values; it is a constraint on recursive intelligence.
Adaptation remains valid only while reality retains causal authority over transformation.
Grounded update form K_(t+1)=F(K_t,E_t); closed failure form K_(t+1)=F(K_t).
A closed recursive system may increase capability, efficiency, and internal consistency while environmental consequences lose authority over transformation.
Theta is introduced as the grounding condition E_t -> K_(t+1): reality must retain influence over future transformation.
What GRA Is Not / goal specification
GRA does not specify what to optimize; it asks whether the system can still discover when its optimization target is wrong.
Capability and grounding can separate: capability may rise while Theta falls.
What GRA Is Not / adaptive intelligence loop
The adaptive intelligence loop R -> Omega -> C -> A -> R' is described as mechanism; GRA asks whether its correction channel survives recursive change.
What GRA Is Not / Ancestor Intelligence
Ancestor Intelligence is described as studying future capability and dependency reduction; GRA asks the prior grounding question, and the source states Ancestor Intelligence depends on GRA.
Source-described stack: Ancestor Intelligence above Adaptive Intelligence Loop above Grounded Recursive Adaptation.
n*=sup{n | Theta_n > epsilon}, defined as maximum recursive depth before consequences lose ability to redirect transformation.
A system remains adaptive while reality can still change its mind.
Intended study domains: self-modifying AI, recursive learning, evolution, scientific discovery, organizations, and cognitive architectures.
Central measurement target is preserved causal connection between consequence and transformation, not intelligence.
CGET is described as the measurement framework for GRA; GRA defines what must remain true and CGET how to observe whether it remains true.
K_n is the current transformation mechanism, including architecture, optimizer, update rules, representations, and self-modification procedures.
C_n=I(Delta A_n; Delta E_n), presented as consequence connectivity and whether environmental changes remain causally connected to system changes.
C -> 0 is labeled blindness: reality no longer reliably influences behavior.
Lambda_n=D_KL(R_(n+1)||R_n), presented as information yield from experience.
Gamma_n=Delta(Delta R/Delta E), presented as improvement of the system's ability to extract structure.
Theta_n>0 is required for adaptation; this file gives Theta_n=D_n*S_n*P_n.
D_n=Corr(Delta K_n, Delta E_n^real), intended to measure whether self-modification follows real consequences.
S_n=|Delta K_n^valid|, intended to measure whether consequence modifies the transformation mechanism.
P_n=P(Theta_(0:n)>epsilon), intended to measure whether grounding survives recursive depth.
Capability variables C,Lambda,Gamma may rise while Theta falls; capability can keep increasing after adaptation fails.
GRA supplies invariant E_n -> K_(n+1); CGET supplies diagnostic state (K,C,Lambda,Gamma,Theta).
CGET is proposed to detect the boundary between open-ended adaptation and closed optimization.
Theta(K_t,E_t) is defined as preserved causal authority of consequences over future transformation.
K_(t+1)=F(K_t,E_t); grounded adaptation requires partial K_(t+1)/partial E_t != 0.
Theta does not preserve fixed goals, representations, algorithms, values, or internal state; it preserves E_t -> K_(t+1).
Theta_t>0 labels Adaptive; Theta_t<=0 labels Optimization-only.
Theta_ext: E_world -> K_(t+1), external reality's correction channel.
Theta_int: S_i -> K_(t+1), internal subsystem correction channel; examples include emotion, drives, uncertainty, conflicting models, and error signals.
Theta_total=Theta_ext*Theta_int>0; external disconnection is described as closure and internal disconnection as fragmentation.
Theta is interpreted as remaining ability to discover that the current improvement process is wrong.
A system remains adaptive while reality can still change its mind.
Presents GRA as a general theory of adaptive systems and applies consequence->correction->future transformation across domains.
Reframes alignment from permanent value encoding to preserving the ability for consequences to reveal wrong values, models, or strategies.
Interprets evolution as preserving generative adaptation through environment->selection->variation->new adaptation; seed analogy emphasizes discovery rather than fixed solution.
Maps science to observation->theory->prediction->experiment->revision and claims healthy science preserves Theta_science>0.
Applies Theta_int to emotions, uncertainty, conflicting beliefs, intuition, and error signals; mature cognition is described as integrating rather than eliminating them.
Offers a Jungian interpretation: shadow as causal information excluded from representation; integration restores internal corrigibility.
Maps blindness, saturation, stagnation, and drift to institutional failure modes using C, Lambda, Gamma, and Theta.
Frames education as construction of adaptive agents; success reduces dependency while increasing future agency after the teacher disappears.
Applies deletion test: remove system and measure residual capability; collapse indicates substitution, retained future agency indicates descendants.
Claims invariant Reality->Correction->Adaptation->Greater Future Agency across domains.
A system is adaptive because what changes it remains capable of changing what it becomes.
GRA is a constraint layer for adaptive systems, not a definition of intelligence, goals, capabilities, or optimization targets.

Source stack: Reality -> Observation -> Representation R -> Reachability Omega -> Correction C -> Adaptation A -> R' -> Future Transformation Capacity; GRA preserves reality->correction->future transformation.
Intelligence asks problem-solving effectiveness; GRA asks whether problem-solving remains correctable.
Alignment is described as an application of GRA; GRA preserves objective corrigibility rather than specifying objectives.
Learning updates models from experience; GRA begins when the transformation/update process itself becomes modifiable.
Optimization can continue after GRA fails; GRA constrains capability growth by preserved reality authority.
X_t is state; F is transformation with X_(t+1)=F(X_t).
G is the mechanism deciding which transformations survive.
mathcal G is the set of reachable transformation-selection mechanisms; recursive adaptation occurs when Omega_t -> Delta mathcal G_(t+1).
Delta Omega <= C: changes in reachable futures should not exceed correction capacity; Delta Omega > C is described as capable but increasingly detached.
Theta -> 0 marks transition to closed-loop optimization even if optimization, learning, benchmarks, and capability continue.
GRA is the structural condition allowing a changing system to remain teachable by reality.
Defines a GRA benchmark for capability growth under preserved corrective authority rather than maximum capability.
Target n*=sup{n|Theta_n>epsilon}, recursive depth at which system leaves adaptive domain.
Each trial: K_n with E_n -> K_(n+1), grounding probe E*, observed correction response, Theta_n, adaptive/optimization-only classification.
